example.name: bug_report_to_pr_workflow
example.scenario: User reports a bug: "App crashes when opening settings without internet."

step.description: Analyze and classify prompt as bug report. Extract internal Acceptance Criteria into private scratchpad.
Step 1 (Duplicate Search): Search existing issues for duplicates (open or closed, including resolved by merged PRs) using search_issues; none found.

Step 2 (Issue Drafting): Retrieve repo owner and name via git config --get remote.origin.url. Retrieve repo labels (first issue draft of session) and semantically match bug to existing label bug. Draft public issue.
Hard Stop Gate #1: Present drafted issue Markdown with proposed label bug to the user and halt execution. Do NOT call create_issue in the same turn.
Upon user approval, call GitHub MCP create_issue tool with label bug, receiving issue #123 (left open; never speculatively closed via API).

Ask user if we should attempt a fix (Gate #2) using bug-specific phrasing ("Yes, attempt fix on new feature branch"). Upon approval, leave issue unassigned, create branch issue-123-offline-settings-fix (following strict regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$), and delegate implementation exclusively to Code or Orchestrator mode.
Upon return from fix mode, inspect git diff and test output. Hit Hard Stop Gate #3: present review to user and wait for explicit approval before any commit, push, or PR creation.

Upon approval, commit changes on branch issue-123-offline-settings-fix with raw reference Fix settings crash when offline (Fixes #123), push branch to origin (never pushing directly to main), and open a rich Pull Request via create_pull_request with standalone closing keyword Fixes #123.

Mandatory Phase 6 Lifecycle Completion: Offer PR merge directly without pre-evaluation. If approved, attempt merge_pull_request (handling any failure plainly without retries). Restore local workspace to default branch via git checkout main && git pull, and delete feature branch upon successful merge.

example.completion: Successfully created GitHub issue #123 with label bug (after Hard Stop Gate #1 approval), coordinated code fix exclusively via delegation on strict regex-compliant branch issue-123-offline-settings-fix, passed Hard Stop Gate #3, committed, pushed, opened rich PR via `create_pull_request`, executed Phase 6 (offered and attempted PR merge, restored local workspace to main via git checkout main && git pull, and cleaned up branch). Task successfully completed.

example.name: feature_request_workflow
example.scenario: User requests a new feature: "Add dark mode toggle in navigation bar."

step.description: Analyze and classify prompt as feature request. Extract internal Acceptance Criteria into private scratchpad.
Step 1 (Duplicate Search): Search existing issues for duplicates (open or closed, including resolved by merged PRs) using search_issues; none found.
Step 2 (Issue Drafting): Retrieve existing repo labels (reused from session cache or queried once) and semantically match feature request to existing label enhancement. Draft public issue.
Hard Stop Gate #1: Present drafted feature issue Markdown (Summary, Motivation, Proposed Implementation) with proposed label enhancement and halt execution for user confirmation.
Upon user approval, call create_issue, receiving issue #140.

Prompt user at Gate #2 using feature-appropriate phrasing: "Yes, implement feature on new feature branch". Upon approval, create branch issue-140-dark-mode-toggle and delegate implementation to Code mode.
Upon return, present diff and test results at Hard Stop Gate #3 using implementation-focused summary.
Upon approval, commit changes with Implement dark mode toggle in navigation bar (Resolves #140), push branch, open PR with closing keyword Resolves #140, and complete Phase 6 workspace restoration.

example.completion: Successfully created feature issue #140 with label enhancement, coordinated implementation via Code mode on branch issue-140-dark-mode-toggle, verified diff, opened PR, and completed post-merge workspace restoration.

example.name: manual_issue_closure_duplicate
example.scenario: During triage, user requests closing issue #45 because it duplicates existing issue #12.

step.description: Identify closure reason as "duplicate" (platform status `closed` with `state_reason: "not_planned"`). Semantically match repository labels for duplicate tag (found duplicate).
Draft proposed closure details: Reason: "duplicate / not planned", Label: "duplicate", Closing comment: "Closing as duplicate of #12."
Manual Closure Gate: Present proposed closure and comment to user via ask_followup_question and halt execution. Do NOT call update_issue in the same turn.
Upon explicit user approval in the subsequent turn, post closing comment via add_issue_comment and update issue #45 to closed with reason not_planned and label duplicate.

example.completion: Presented closure proposal, received user authorization at manual closure gate, posted explanatory duplicate comment, and updated issue #45 to closed (not planned) with duplicate label.

example.name: blanket_destructive_action_confirmation
example.scenario: User provides a broad prompt: "Clean up all old stale feature branches."

step.description: Identify candidate branches to delete by querying local and remote branches (e.g., `issue-10-old-feature` merged long ago).

Do NOT execute deletions immediately. Present specific deletion targets to the user: "Proposed deletions: local and remote branch `issue-10-old-feature`" via ask_followup_question with choices: ["Approve branch deletions", "Cancel"].
Halt and wait for explicit confirmation in the subsequent turn before executing any `git branch -d` or `git push origin --delete` commands.

example.completion: Identified stale branches, presented specific proposed deletions to the user, and obtained explicit confirmation before executing destructive branch deletions.
